title: One Ångström in Svante Pääbo's Cleanroom — 1856 Feldhofer Valley Neanderthal Bones, <60-bp Ancient DNA Terminal C->T Deamination Smiles & Single-Stranded UDG Base-Flipping (PDB 1EMH), FOXP2 & X-Chromosome Introgression Deserts (PDB 2A07), Antiviral OAS1 (PDB 4IG8) & Neanderthal SCN9A NaV1.7 Pain Gain (PDB 6J8J, 7W9K)

teenKit.tldr: If you are of non-African descent, your cells carry 1 to 2 percent Neanderthal DNA, meaning roughly 40 percent of the extinct Neanderthal genome survives scattered across living humans today. Svante Pääbo and modern geneticists unlocked this invisible history by recovering highly degraded ancient DNA from 40,000-year-old bones.
teenKit.whyItMatters: Those ancient phantom genes are not just museum artifacts; they actively shape your everyday biology, controlling everything from how your immune system fights off modern viruses to how acutely you feel physical pain.
keyTakeaways: Living humans collectively carry about 40% of the entire Neanderthal nuclear genome tiled across global populations, proving Neanderthals never truly went completely extinct.
Ancient DNA degrades into tiny, damaged fragments over tens of thousands of years, requiring brilliant chemical work like single-stranded UDG base-flipping to read accurately.
Neanderthal gene introgression directly impacts modern human traits, including antiviral defenses via OAS1 and heightened pain sensitivity through the SCN9A NaV1.7 channel.

vocab.meaning: The transfer of genetic material from one species into the gene pool of another by repeated backcrossing.
An ultra-tiny unit of measurement equal to one ten-billionth of a meter, used to examine molecular structures.
A chemical breakdown process where ancient DNA loses an amino group over millennia, causing signature mutations.
An enzyme used by scientists to flip out and excise damaged bases in ancient DNA so it can be sequenced correctly.

quiz.question: Approximately what percentage of the total Neanderthal genome survives collectively across living humans today?
quiz.explanation: While each individual carries only 1-2%, different people carry different segments, adding up to roughly 40% of the Neanderthal genome tiled across the global population.

quiz.question: What major obstacle did Svante Pääbo and his team have to overcome to sequence Neanderthal genomes?
options: Severe chemical degradation and fragmentation of ancient DNA
Neanderthal DNA being completely identical to modern human DNA
quiz.explanation: Over 40 millennia, ancient DNA breaks down into short, heavily damaged fragments riddled with chemical alterations like terminal C-to-T deamination.

quiz.question: Which modern human trait is directly influenced by inherited Neanderthal DNA as discussed in the episode?
quiz.explanation: Neanderthal introgression gifted modern humans specific functional genes like OAS1 for antiviral defense and SCN9A NaV1.7 for pain perception.
